c11_bs_cbse_09_010: A tax holiday is temporary and covers only income tax — not GST or TDS. Check: which taxes still apply?
c11_bs_cbse_10_001: Internal trade means within the nation — Delhi to Mumbai is still internal. Check: did a national border get crossed?
c11_bs_cbse_10_002: Breaking bulk is dividing quantity — grading sorts by quality. Check: did you split kilos or sort them?
c11_bs_cbse_10_003: A huge hypermarket selling to households is still retail — the buyer's identity decides, not shop size. Check: who's the end buyer?
c11_bs_cbse_10_004: Street traders have no fixed structure; stall holders do — same street, different category. Check: is there a fixed stall?
c11_bs_cbse_10_005: A big village store is still small-scale — it's the structure, like chains and centralised buying, that counts. Check: who does the buying?
c11_bs_cbse_10_006: A departmental store is centralised buying plus decentralised sales with full service — not a supermarket. Check: self-service or service-heavy?
c11_bs_cbse_10_007: Chain stores sell one narrow range across many branches — wide variety makes it a departmental store. Check: one line or many?
c11_bs_cbse_10_008: Mail order runs through the post — catalogues, VPP, slow returns — not the internet. Check: how does the order travel?
c11_bs_cbse_10_009: Supermarkets trade service for low prices — credit and home delivery belong to departmental stores. Check: who carries your bags?
c11_bs_cbse_10_010: Chambers lobby the government — they don't enforce laws on business. Check: who made the rule?
c11_bs_cbse_10_011: Wholesale isn't just a lower price — it's selling bulk for resale to traders. Check: resale or personal use?
c11_bs_cbse_11_001: International business is more than shipping goods — services, capital and licences cross borders too. Check: did anything physical move?
c11_bs_cbse_11_002: Foreign exchange earnings help the nation, not the firm's P&L — keep the actors separate. Check: nation or firm benefit?
c11_bs_cbse_11_003: Contract manufacturing outsources production; licensing hands over IP for a royalty. Check: what was transferred?
c11_bs_cbse_11_004: The export house is your agent — ownership and payment risk stay with you until the buyer pays. Check: who holds title?
c11_bs_cbse_11_005: The contract factory only makes to spec — it can't sell your brand itself. Check: who owns the marketing?
c11_bs_cbse_11_006: In licensing the partner sells under the brand for a royalty — in contract manufacturing it just makes. Check: who bears market risk?
c11_bs_cbse_11_007: A JV needn't be 50:50, and a wholly-owned subsidiary can be bought, not just built. Check: greenfield or acquisition?
c11_bs_cbse_11_008: A Bill of Entry is filed by the importer — the exporter never touches it. Check: import or export side?
c11_bs_cbse_11_009: The WTO can't strike down laws — it only authorises the winner to retaliate. Check: who enforces the ruling?
c11_bs_cbse_11_010: A trade deficit can reflect essential imports — and export schemes remit taxes, not subsidise. Check: what's driving the gap?
c11_bs_cbse_11_011: International business isn't only exports — think licensing, FDI and political risk too. Check: do any goods cross a border?
c11_chem_cbse_01_001: Chemistry isn't confined to labs — your phone case, DNA nitrogen and toothpaste were designed by it. Check: what object has no chemistry?
c11_chem_cbse_01_002: Mass didn't vanish — the CO2 escaped your weighing; count every phase. Check: did you include the gas?
c11_chem_cbse_01_003: Multiple proportions compares across compounds, not inside one — fix one element's mass first. Check: which mass did you fix?
c11_chem_cbse_01_004: Gay-Lussac ratios are gas volumes at the same T and P — not masses, not liquids. Check: same conditions?
c11_chem_cbse_01_005: Isotopes don't disprove Dalton — his postulate was about chemical sameness, not nuclear identity. Check: chemical or nuclear claim?
c11_chem_cbse_01_006: 12.011 is a ratio, not one atom's grams — atomic mass is dimensionless, molar mass is g/mol. Check: what are the units?
c11_chem_cbse_01_007: NaCl doesn't come in molecules — it's a lattice, so count formula units. Check: molecule or formula unit?
c11_chem_cbse_01_008: H2 weighs double H — use 2.016 g/mol for the molecule. Check: atom or molecule?
c11_chem_cbse_01_009: Percent composition is by mass, not atom count — oxygen outweighs hydrogen in water. Check: atoms or grams?
c11_chem_cbse_01_010: Get the empirical formula before dividing molar mass — CH2O first, then scale up. Check: what's the empirical mass?
c11_chem_cbse_01_011: The coefficients count moles, not grams — convert mass to moles first. Check: did you divide by molar mass?
c11_chem_cbse_01_012: Smaller mass doesn't mean limiting — divide moles by the coefficient to compare. Check: which ratio is smaller?
c11_chem_cbse_01_013: Don't dissolve in 250 mL — dissolve, then make the volume up to 250 mL. Check: solvent volume or solution volume?
c11_chem_cbse_01_014: Molality divides by solvent kilograms — not total solution mass. Check: which mass went on the bottom?
c11_chem_cbse_01_015: Molarity tracks solution litres; molality tracks solvent kilos — they drift apart when dense. Check: which is temperature-proof?
c11_chem_cbse_02_001: Cathode rays bend in electric and magnetic fields — waves wouldn't; they're charged particles. Check: does the beam deflect?
c11_chem_cbse_02_002: The field does no work, yet the circle's radius still hands you e/m. Check: what does r reveal?
